chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
If something from the urine of the cat gets onto the garment, then salat (prayer) in it is not valid until you wash it.

key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing on which impurity may fall
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity depends here on purity of clothing
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine, the substance causing ritual impurity here
key_terms.تَغْسِلَهُ: you wash it, meaning cleansing the garment from the impurity

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in a garment contaminated with cat urine?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ritual purity of clothing for salat (prayer). It states that if cat urine touches a garment, salat (prayer) in that garment is not valid until the impurity is washed away.
